back: A list of the assets and liabilities of a business at a date; the difference is the owner's capital.
Closing capital - opening capital + drawings - capital introduced.
Assets = capital + liabilities, so capital = assets - liabilities.
Drawings reduced closing capital but are not an expense, so they are added back to find the profit that was earned.
New money from the owner raises capital but is not earned profit.

front: Effect of overvalued closing inventory on estimated profit
back: Closing capital and profit are overstated by the same amount.

front: Limitations of the statement of affairs method
back: One profit figure only, no detail of sales and costs, errors undetected, reliance on estimates and memory.

front: A negative result in the capital formula
back: It means a loss for the year.

front: Is the capital in a statement of affairs ever negative?
back: Yes, if liabilities exceed assets: the business owes more than it owns.
